turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
I came in because I just can't stop thinking about how the left side of my face looks off. It's like my nose and my jaw are crooked. Every time I see an ID photo or look at the camera for my online classes, it's just really obvious to me. 

People tell me they don't see it when I bring it up, but... I just feel like everyone in the CNC lab is noticing it. It feels like they're staring at my face before they even notice my work, and it's just really getting to me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent preoccupation with perceived crookedness in their nose and jaw that others state they do not see, causing significant distress.

turns.doctor_question: When people tell you they don't notice any asymmetry, do you think it's possible they're right and you're just overly focused on a minor flaw, or do you feel certain that the defect is really there exactly as you see it?
turns.patient_response: I... I know they say they don't see it, but I just don't believe them. I feel like they're just being polite or trying to make me feel better. When I look in the mirror or see those photos, it's right there. It's not a minor thing to me. I'm certain it's exactly as bad as I see it. It's just so obvious.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from your concerns about your face, have you noticed any other unusual thoughts, beliefs, or experiences—like feeling that people are talking about you for other reasons, or sensing things that others don't seem to notice?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, I don't hear things or see things that aren't there, and I don't think people are talking about me for any other reason. It's really just... just my face. That's the only thing that's bothering me. I just feel like that's what everyone is looking at when they see me. But other than that, no, nothing unusual.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms ongoing preoccupation with their facial appearance, stating their face is the only thing bothering them and feeling that everyone is looking at it.
symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies delusions or referential beliefs, stating they do not believe people are talking about them for any other reason.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient clearly denies hallucinations, stating they do not hear or see things that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself frequently checking your face in mirrors or photos, trying to hide or cover that side of your face, or avoiding situations like video calls or cameras because of how it looks?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Every morning before I leave for school, I get stuck in the bathroom just... checking my face in the mirror. I use my phone camera, too, to check the angles. I spend a lot of time fixing my hair or changing my shirts to see if it hides it better. I usually end up asking my mom if it looks weird, too. It takes up so much time that sometimes I completely miss my lab, or... or by the time I actually get there, I'm just too wiped out to even focus on my work.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive appearance-related behaviors, including mirror and phone camera checking, camouflaging with hair and clothing, and seeking reassurance from their mother.
